name: Erdős–Rado Sunflower Conjecture
headline: For each r≥3, ∃C_r so every k-uniform set family of size >C_r^k contains an r-sunflower.
first: For all k,m≥2, every k-uniform family F contains F' with |F'|≥c_k m^(-k)|F| and each intersection of two distinct F' members is a kernel of an m-petal sunflower wholly within F'.
risk: The 2026 question may be almost as hard as the target; k=3 must be separately audited.
applications: B: restricted-intersection bounds and quantum shadow tomography via published delta-system tools; not deployment-ready.
ladder: Resolve or improve the internal-witness quantitative delta-system extraction question of Janzer et al. (2026 §6).
Prove sharp extraction/obstruction structure for fixed k or structured hypergraphs.
Obtain single-exponential quantitative internal-kernel results for an infinite parameter family.
Develop new robust sunflower extraction that removes a major log(k) loss for broad families.
Prove the unrestricted Erdős–Rado sunflower conjecture.

name: Rota's Basis Conjecture
headline: Every n labeled rank-n matroid bases can be rearranged into n disjoint transversal bases.
first: Unrestricted rank-five transversal basis decomposition for every rank-five matroid, with labeled occurrences.
risk: Rank-five open-status not directly established; earlier formalisation competition exists.
applications: C: constructive base packing may inform matroid algorithms and scheduling, not a direct consequence of existence.
ladder: Audit then resolve unrestricted rank-five case.
Derive novel exchange/obstruction reduction for bounded ranks.
Prove a uniform infinite family of matroid classes.
Close exact packing–covering gap for a substantial matroid family.
Prove Rota's Basis Conjecture in all ranks.

name: MDS Conjecture for Linear Codes
headline: For nontrivial linear [N,k] MDS codes over F_q, N≤q+1 except the standard even-q k=3 or dual exceptions with N≤q+2.
first: Find a new provable residual dimension range for composite q beyond the bounds claimed by Fan (2026), after auditing that preprint.
risk: 2026 dramatic dimension-range preprint must be checked; algebraic competition intense.
applications: A: MDS codes support error correction and distributed storage; longer hypothetical parameters do not directly improve deployed codes.
ladder: Audit and enlarge a residual dimension/field regime.
Classify critical arcs or determinant obstructions.
Prove a new infinite extension-field range.
Combine obstruction theories near the remaining middle dimensions.
Prove the full linear MDS conjecture.

name: Planar k-set Extremal Problem
headline: Determine tight asymptotic maximum of k-sets of n planar points in general position.
first: Improve a published bound in a precisely frozen nontrivial regime of k and n; exact improvement not yet specified.
risk: No independently checked 2025–26 sharp comparator; proposed first-paper target not frozen.
applications: B: complexity analysis of levels and geometric algorithms; not an automatic improvement to deployed software.
ladder: Isolate an unsolved restricted k-level incidence bound.
Derive structural crossing/charging lemma.
Extend to a growing k-regime or pseudoline arrangements.
Narrow exponent gap between upper and lower k-set bounds.
Resolve sharp planar k-set extremal order.

name: Frankl's Union-Closed Sets Conjecture
headline: Every nontrivial finite union-closed family has an element occurring in at least half of its members.
first: Prove a new 1/2-frequency result for a structurally defined non-subsumed family of Horn Boolean systems.
risk: Exact Horn subclass has not been frozen and may be subsumed; latest October 2026 entropy threshold is moving.
applications: B: Horn Boolean functions and entropy inequalities; specific operational gains speculative.
ladder: Establish a substantive new restricted-class half-frequency theorem.
Classify minimal counterexample structural certificates.
Unify tractable Horn/semilattice subclasses.
Find beyond-entropy global structural decomposition.
Prove Frankl's conjecture.

name: Caccetta–Häggkvist Directed Girth Conjecture
headline: A simple n-vertex digraph of minimum outdegree ≥r has directed girth at most ceil(n/r).
first: Extend an explicitly sourced small-independence theorem to a larger exact regime without subsumption.
risk: 2019 result not a current status audit; much recent graph activity unexamined.
applications: C: directed network feedback-cycle guarantees, no certified engineering performance.
ladder: Prove new expansion/girth regime.
Develop short-cycle neighborhood certificate.
Generalise to a natural infinite digraph class.
Resolve r=n/3 or another major intermediate frontier.
Prove full Caccetta–Häggkvist.

name: Lonely Runner Conjecture
headline: For any k positive integer velocities, ∃t with all ||t u_i||≥1/(k+1).
first: Certify or prove the 14-runner case (k=13) after auditing 2026 certificates and any subsequent claims.
risk: April/September 2026 preprint claims up to 13 runners, so prior smaller targets are superseded.
applications: C: periodic scheduling and simultaneous approximation analogies; no demonstrated transfer.
ladder: Resolve or reduce the next k=13 case.
Develop new exact minimal-counterexample sieves.
Prove infinitely many structured velocity families.
Obtain an effective uniform-in-k lower separation law.
Prove the Lonely Runner Conjecture.

name: Matrix Multiplication Exponent 2
headline: Prove the exponent ω of square matrix multiplication equals 2.
first: Prove a new rigorous optimization/certificate inequality improving an explicitly current tensor-method bound, without duplicate AlphaEvolve output.
risk: 2026 industrial AI competition and sophisticated computational optimization make accessible novel improvements unlikely.
applications: B: genuine algorithmic complexity implications; weak direct practical crossover for huge tensor constructions.
ladder: Novel independently checked optimization inequality.
New certified tensor degeneration/laser-method obstruction.
Family-wide rectangular multiplication improvement.
Break a substantive barrier in arithmetic tensor methods.
Establish ω=2.

name: Beck–Fiala Discrepancy Conjecture
headline: Sparse incidence matrix columns of support ≤t admit ±1 signing with row discrepancy O(sqrt(t)).
first: Independent formal/mathematical verification of Guo–Fang–Lu's claimed 2026 constant-bound proof, not an original proof of the conjecture.
risk: September 2026 arXiv preprint explicitly claims resolution; cannot advertise original theorem opportunity.
applications: B: balancing, rounding, sparse optimisation; application bounds do not imply practical software.
ladder: Audit claimed resolution and formal trust assumptions.
Develop reusable formal vector-balancing components.
Explore constructive algorithmic extraction from an existence proof.
Prove algorithmic complexity gains not already known.
Claimed conjecture resolution must be verified, not rediscovered.

name: Twin Prime Conjecture
headline: There are infinitely many primes p with p+2 also prime.
first: Obtain a new unconditional nonroutine sieve result for pair correlations with a precisely stated improvement over published comparators.
risk: Sieve parity obstruction and tiny accessible proof window; weak direct practical value.
applications: D: no demonstrated practical value of infinite twin-prime existence.
ladder: Novel unconditional sieve/correlation estimate.
Extend the estimate to prime-pair families.
New parity-breaking ingredient for an infinite class.
Obtain unconditionally arbitrarily small even prime gaps.
Prove infinitely many twin primes.
